blocks.text: The daily administrative grind for event coordinators

Your day as an event coordinator often feels like a constant battle against a growing list of tasks. You manage vendor contracts, coordinate room blocks, and update attendee lists in real time. Most of this work happens inside a web browser or a dedicated desktop app. When you switch between these tools, you lose time finding buttons or remembering specific menu paths.

Many planners report working 15 to 20 hour days during peak event cycles. This exhaustion often comes from the repetitive nature of the work. If you have to update a schedule, you might need to change it in your project management software, your email templates, and your shared calendar. Each step is a chance for a mistake or a delay.
Using your Mac for event management

Your Mac is a powerful hub for your event planning checklist. You likely use apps like Trello or Asana for task tracking, and Slack for team communication. The challenge is keeping these apps synced with your mental state. When you are deep in a task, you do not want to stop to search for a setting or a specific file.
Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask Lazur where a specific setting is in your browser. It will draw a circle around the button so you do not have to hunt for it.

blocks.text: The most common mistake is manual redundancy. If you track attendee dietary requirements in a spreadsheet and then copy them into an email, you are doing double the work. Use your Mac to keep these files in one place. If you are handling sensitive data, ensure you follow your company policies regarding data privacy.
How to use your checklist with Lazur

Administrative burden can push your work hours to 80 percent of your total time for complex events. You need to identify which tasks can be automated or handled faster. Simple things like setting timers for vendor follow-ups or checking your calendar can be done by voice. This leaves you more time for the creative parts of your job.

When you use AI tools, you must be careful with sensitive attendee information. Lazur is built with privacy in mind. It only listens and looks at your screen while you hold the shortcut key. Your data is not stored, and it is never used to train AI models. Always check your employer's rules before using any new software with client or vendor data.
